3	
4	## LRN-2026-08-24-c: A client-asserted identity is a claim, not a proof -- cryptographic verification is required the moment an action is account-scoped and irreversible
5	
6	```meta
7	date: 2026-08-24
8	project: arcade-web
9	stack: [angular, amplify-gen2, dynamodb, cognito, lambda-function-url]
10	req: [REQ-ARC-14]
11	auditor_run: frontend/AUDIT_REPORT.md@2026-08-24
12	severity: HIGH
13	origin: crew-auditor
14	```
15	
16	**What happened:** REQ-ARC-14's scout contract recommended trusting a body-passed `sub`, "verified" only by confirming the caller held some valid signed credential -- the SAME trust model this codebase's other platform functions already use for their client-asserted `identityId`. An operator ruling overrode this as forgeable: any signed caller (even a guest's own valid credentials) could assert another account's `sub` in the body and permanently steal a resource tied to it. The fix cryptographically verifies the caller's Cognito ID token against the pool's JWKS and acts only on the token's own verified claim. The auditor independently re-attacked the deployed endpoint: forged/tampered/missing tokens all rejected at 401; a forged `sub` riding alongside a real token was structurally unreachable (the handler never parses it); and a real token submitted while a *different* identity's credentials did the IAM signing still resolved to the token's own account, never the signer's -- proving the two trust layers (coarse IAM signing, fine-grained token verification) are genuinely independent and composable, not redundant.
17	
18	**Why it matters:** most authenticated actions in a system are fine with "some valid signed caller" as the whole trust model -- a guest's own pairing, moves, and presence are self-contained to that one session and cost nothing if merely coarse-grained. The trust model silently stops being sufficient the instant an action's correctness depends on WHICH specific account is calling AND its effect is durable/hard-to-reverse (here: permanent, exclusive ownership). Reusing the codebase's existing, working trust pattern by default is the natural move and was exactly the wrong one here.
19	
20	**Pattern to encode:** before trusting any client-asserted identity field (a body `sub`, a JWT claim read without signature verification, a session id used as if it were proof), ask: does this action's correctness depend on WHICH identity is calling (not just "some" valid one), and is the effect account-scoped and durable/irreversible? If yes to both, the identity must be cryptographically verified server-side against its own issuer (JWKS/JWT verification, not "the caller holds a valid credential for some other coarser-grained gate"), and the verified claim -- never a request-body field of the same name -- is the only thing the handler may act on.
21	
22	## LRN-2026-08-22-a: 100% coverage does not prove a signal-exposed WS message type is actually consumed by the UI
23	
24	```meta
25	date: 2026-08-22
26	project: arcade-web
27	stack: [angular, vitest, websocket, signals]
28	req: [REQ-ARC-7]
29	auditor_run: frontend/AUDIT_REPORT.md@2026-08-22
30	severity: blocker
31	```
32	
33	**What happened.** `GameSocketService` (the coder-spec's mandated single owning service for `/ws/game`) correctly exposed all seven server-to-client message types as readonly signals, including `moveError`. The tester wrote a passing unit test asserting `moveError()` updates when a `move_error` frame arrives. Coverage reported 100% line/branch/function on the service and on every component. But no component ever read `gameSocket.moveError()` -- the handoff contract's documented UI action ("transient rejection cue: shake the cell, toast the message; route non-recoverable codes to an error state") was never built. The auditor found this only by grepping for the signal's call sites outside test files, not from any tool output.
34	
35	**Why it matters.** Coverage tools measure whether producer-side code executed, not whether a consumer exists downstream. A well-tested, fully-covered signal or observable can be entirely dead from the user's perspective while every quality gate reports green. This is structurally invisible to line/branch coverage because there is no untaken branch -- the producer code runs fine every time.
36	
37	**Pattern to encode.** When a spec mandates a service expose "every message type as a signal" (fan-out architecture), the audit checklist must separately verify each exposed signal has at least one non-test call site, not just that the producer path is covered. Grep for `<signalName>(` outside `*.spec.ts` as a cheap first pass before trusting coverage numbers on message-routing services.
38	
39	## LRN-2026-08-22-i: Exhaustive per-value test coverage belongs at the layer that branches on the value, not the layer that merely passes it through
40	
41	```meta
42	date: 2026-08-22
43	project: arcade-web
44	stack: [angular, vitest, websocket]
45	req: [REQ-ARC-7]
46	auditor_run: frontend/AUDIT_REPORT.md@2026-08-22
47	severity: suggestion
48	```
49	
50	**What happened.** A prior audit suggested a service-layer WS-message spec should parameterize over all 7 members of a discriminated-union code field, since it only tested 2 directly. A later fix exhaustively covered all 7 at the consumer layer (the component that maps each code to distinct UI text) instead. Re-examining the service's actual routing code showed it performs zero per-code branching -- it stores the whole message object regardless of which of the 7 values arrived. Parameterizing the service spec over all 7 values would have tested nothing the 2-value spec did not already prove; the router doesn't care which value it is.
51	
52	**Why it matters.** "Only N of M enum values are tested at this layer" is not automatically a gap. Whether it is a gap depends on whether that layer's code varies its behavior by value. Flagging it reflexively, without checking for branching, sends fix effort to the wrong file and can produce redundant tests that inflate a suite without adding assurance.
53	
54	**Pattern to encode.** Before treating partial per-value coverage as a finding, check whether the flagged code path branches on the value at all. If it's a pure pass-through, the exhaustive check belongs at the nearest layer that actually discriminates.

id: REQ-ARC-3
title: Game rules and server authority
priority: 3
depends_on: [REQ-ARC-2]
status: pending
---

## Requirement
The server is the sole authority on the board. It decides every move's legality and every outcome; a client can never make an illegal move stick or fabricate a result.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Only the player whose turn it is may move, and only to an empty cell in the 3x3 grid; any other attempt is rejected with a specific reason and leaves the board unchanged.
2. A player who is not a participant of a game cannot affect it.
3. A win is detected on any of the 8 lines (3 rows, 3 columns, 2 diagonals) and names the winner and the winning line; a full board with no line is a draw.
4. A finished game is immutable: no further move changes it.
5. The authoritative game state (board, whose turn, participants, result) can be read at any time and is the source of truth over any live notification.
```

**Criterion→test map** (all in `amplify/shared/game-rules.spec.ts`; full test names are in the tracking log)
- **AC1:** the "applyMove turn and cell legality" block covers these cases:
  - **Accepted moves:** a valid move and turn flip, boundary cells 0 and 8, and no mutation of the input state.
  - **Wrong turn:** out of turn, and the same player moving twice.
  - **Bad cell:** an occupied cell, and cells -1, 9, 1.5, NaN, Infinity and 100.
  - **Check order:** wrong turn is reported before an invalid cell.
  - **Unchanged state:** every rejection compares the input state against a pre-call snapshot.
- **AC2:** the "applyMove non-participants" block covers these cases:
  - **Game stage:** an outsider on a fresh, in-progress and finished game.
  - **Odd inputs:** an outsider with an invalid cell, the case-different id 'Alice', and an empty id.
  - **Check:** each asserts `not_a_participant` with the state unchanged.
- **AC3:**
  - **Winning lines:** `findWinningLine` and `applyMove` are each run over all 8 lines for both marks (16 cases each). The expected lines are written independently of `WINNING_LINES`.
  - **No win:** `findWinningLine` returns null for an empty board, two-in-a-row, and mixed lines.
  - **Real games:** one X win and one O win.
  - **Line table:** `WINNING_LINES` is checked to contain exactly the 3 rows, 3 columns and 2 diagonals.
  - **Draw:** a full board with no line is a draw, and a board with an empty cell is not.
  - **Ninth move:** a win completed on the ninth move scores as a win, not a draw.
- **AC4:** the "finished games are immutable" block runs after both a won and a drawn game:
  - **Either participant:** a further move is rejected with `game_finished`.
  - **Occupied cell:** a move onto an occupied cell is also `game_finished`.
  - **Invalid cell:** a move to an invalid cell is also `game_finished`.
  - **Extra cases:** a won game that still has empty cells, and a state where `turn` is null with no result.
- **AC5:** the `readAuthoritativeState` block covers these cases:
  - **Field equality:** the copy equals the source on a fresh game.
  - **Tracking moves:** the read reflects each accepted move, and a rejected move leaves it unchanged.
  - **Results:** it exposes the win result and the draw result.
  - **Frozen copy:** the copy is deeply frozen, and writing to it throws `TypeError`.
  - **Independence:** a later mutation of the source does not leak into the read.
  - **Not testable here:** the "source of truth over a live notification" half belongs to the server layer. This module has no notification code.
- **Extra (not an AC):** `createGame` is tested for its initial state and for the `RangeError` on empty or identical ids.

Every rejection goes through `expectRejected`, which deep-compares the input state with a pre-call snapshot.
    - AC2: `applyMove non-participants` > outsider on fresh game, in-progress game, finished game; outsider with an invalid cell; case-different id ('Alice'); empty id. Each asserts `not_a_participant` and an unchanged state.
    - AC3: `win detection` > "findWinningLine detects $label" and "applyMove names winner and line for $label" (16 cases each: 8 lines x X/O, expected lines written independently of `WINNING_LINES`), "returns null" cases, real X-win and O-win games; `WINNING_LINES` > "lists exactly the 3 rows, 3 columns and 2 diagonals"; `draw detection` > "declares a draw on a full board with no line", "does not declare a draw while a cell is still empty", "scores a line completed on the ninth move as a win, not a draw".

    - AC5: `readAuthoritativeState` > "returns fields equal to the source state for a fresh game", "reflects each accepted move", "is unchanged by a rejected move", "exposes the win result with winner and line", "exposes the draw result", "returns a deeply frozen copy", "freezes the draw result too", "throws when a caller writes to the returned copy, leaving the source intact", "is a copy: later mutation of the source board does not leak into the read". Not testable here: the "source of truth over a live notification" half of AC5 is a server-layer concern (no notification code exists in this module), per the scout contract.
    - Extra (not an AC): `createGame` > initial state and RangeError for empty or identical ids.
- **Files changed:** `amplify/shared/game-rules.ts` (new; types, `WINNING_LINES`, `createGame`, `findWinningLine`, `applyMove`, `readAuthoritativeState`).
- **Verification:** `npx tsc -p amplify/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; `npx eslint amplify/shared/game-rules.ts` clean. No ampx or AWS command run.
- **Gate-fix (coder, 2026-10-28, condition 2):** `ng test` now discovers `amplify/**/*.spec.ts`. Changes: `angular.json` `projects.*.architect.test.options.include` = `["**/*.spec.ts", "../amplify/**/*.spec.ts"]` (the unit-test builder resolves globs relative to `sourceRoot` = `src`, so a plain `amplify/**` pattern matched nothing; `../amplify` escapes it); `tsconfig.spec.json` `include` gained `"amplify/**/*.spec.ts"` so the specs are type-checked with the spec tsconfig. `vitest.config.ts` unchanged (generated-file coverage excludes kept). Result: `npx ng test --watch=false` -> 2 files, 86 tests pass; `--coverage` -> amplify/shared/game-rules.ts statements 100% (33/33), branches 100% (40/40), functions 100% (5/5), lines 100% (32/32); overall 100%. ## Requirement
The server is the sole authority on the board. It decides every move's legality and every outcome; a client can never make an illegal move stick or fabricate a result.

1. Only the player whose turn it is may move, and only to an empty cell in the 3x3 grid; any other attempt is rejected with a specific reason and leaves the board unchanged.

4. A finished game is immutable: no further move changes it.
5. The authoritative game state (board, whose turn, participants, result) can be read at any time and is the source of truth over any live notification.

62	```ts
63	export const WINNING_LINES: readonly WinningLine[];   // exactly 8 entries: 3 rows, 3 cols, 2 diagonals
64	
65	export function createGame(participants: { readonly X: PlayerId; readonly O: PlayerId }): GameState;

67	// Not an AC, so at most one test if implemented.

69	export function findWinningLine(board: Board): { readonly mark: Mark; readonly line: WinningLine } | null;
70	// Scans WINNING_LINES in array order; returns the first all-same non-null line, else null.
71	
72	export function applyMove(state: GameState, move: Move): MoveOutcome;
73	// Pure. Never mutates `state` or `move`. Returns a new GameState on success.
74	// On rejection returns { ok: false, reason } and NO state. The caller keeps its stored state.

76	export function readAuthoritativeState(state: GameState): GameState;

82	
83	- `turn` is `null` if and only if `result` is non-null.
84	- A win sets `result = { outcome: 'win', winner, winnerId, line }`, where `winnerId = participants[winner]` and `line` is the matching `WINNING_LINES` entry.
85	- A draw sets `result = { outcome: 'draw' }`. This happens only when the board is full and `findWinningLine` returns null.

90	1. `not_a_participant`: `move.playerId` matches neither `participants.X` nor `participants.O`. This runs first so outsiders learn nothing about the game's status.

93	4. `invalid_cell`: `!Number.isInteger(cell) || cell < 0 || cell > 8`.
94	5. `cell_occupied`: `board[cell] !== null`.

1	# relevant_learnings for REQ-ARC-3 (advisory; specs win on any conflict)
2	# Graded by crew-evaluator: 0 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM. Entries below are verbatim.
3	
4	## LRN-2026-08-24-c: A client-asserted identity is a claim, not a proof -- cryptographic verification is required the moment an action is account-scoped and irreversible
5	
6	```meta
7	date: 2026-08-24
8	project: arcade-web
9	stack: [angular, amplify-gen2, dynamodb, cognito, lambda-function-url]
10	req: [REQ-ARC-14]
11	auditor_run: frontend/AUDIT_REPORT.md@2026-08-24
12	severity: HIGH
13	origin: crew-auditor
14	```
15	
16	**What happened:** REQ-ARC-14's scout contract recommended trusting a body-passed `sub`, "verified" only by confirming the caller held some valid signed credential -- the SAME trust model this codebase's other platform functions already use for their client-asserted `identityId`. An operator ruling overrode this as forgeable: any signed caller (even a guest's own valid credentials) could assert another account's `sub` in the body and permanently steal a resource tied to it. The fix cryptographically verifies the caller's Cognito ID token against the pool's JWKS and acts only on the token's own verified claim. The auditor independently re-attacked the deployed endpoint: forged/tampered/missing tokens all rejected at 401; a forged `sub` riding alongside a real token was structurally unreachable (the handler never parses it); and a real token submitted while a *different* identity's credentials did the IAM signing still resolved to the token's own account, never the signer's -- proving the two trust layers (coarse IAM signing, fine-grained token verification) are genuinely independent and composable, not redundant.
17	
18	**Why it matters:** most authenticated actions in a system are fine with "some valid signed caller" as the whole trust model -- a guest's own pairing, moves, and presence are self-contained to that one session and cost nothing if merely coarse-grained. The trust model silently stops being sufficient the instant an action's correctness depends on WHICH specific account is calling AND its effect is durable/hard-to-reverse (here: permanent, exclusive ownership). Reusing the codebase's existing, working trust pattern by default is the natural move and was exactly the wrong one here.
19	
20	**Pattern to encode:** before trusting any client-asserted identity field (a body `sub`, a JWT claim read without signature verification, a session id used as if it were proof), ask: does this action's correctness depend on WHICH identity is calling (not just "some" valid one), and is the effect account-scoped and durable/irreversible? If yes to both, the identity must be cryptographically verified server-side against its own issuer (JWKS/JWT verification, not "the caller holds a valid credential for some other coarser-grained gate"), and the verified claim -- never a request-body field of the same name -- is the only thing the handler may act on.
21	
22	## LRN-2026-08-22-a: 100% coverage does not prove a signal-exposed WS message type is actually consumed by the UI
23	
24	```meta
25	date: 2026-08-22
26	project: arcade-web
27	stack: [angular, vitest, websocket, signals]
28	req: [REQ-ARC-7]
29	auditor_run: frontend/AUDIT_REPORT.md@2026-08-22
30	severity: blocker
31	```
32	
33	**What happened.** `GameSocketService` (the coder-spec's mandated single owning service for `/ws/game`) correctly exposed all seven server-to-client message types as readonly signals, including `moveError`. The tester wrote a passing unit test asserting `moveError()` updates when a `move_error` frame arrives. Coverage reported 100% line/branch/function on the service and on every component. But no component ever read `gameSocket.moveError()` -- the handoff contract's documented UI action ("transient rejection cue: shake the cell, toast the message; route non-recoverable codes to an error state") was never built. The auditor found this only by grepping for the signal's call sites outside test files, not from any tool output.
34	
35	**Why it matters.** Coverage tools measure whether producer-side code executed, not whether a consumer exists downstream. A well-tested, fully-covered signal or observable can be entirely dead from the user's perspective while every quality gate reports green. This is structurally invisible to line/branch coverage because there is no untaken branch -- the producer code runs fine every time.
36	
37	**Pattern to encode.** When a spec mandates a service expose "every message type as a signal" (fan-out architecture), the audit checklist must separately verify each exposed signal has at least one non-test call site, not just that the producer path is covered. Grep for `<signalName>(` outside `*.spec.ts` as a cheap first pass before trusting coverage numbers on message-routing services.
38	
39	## LRN-2026-08-22-i: Exhaustive per-value test coverage belongs at the layer that branches on the value, not the layer that merely passes it through
40	
41	```meta
42	date: 2026-08-22
43	project: arcade-web
44	stack: [angular, vitest, websocket]
45	req: [REQ-ARC-7]
46	auditor_run: frontend/AUDIT_REPORT.md@2026-08-22
47	severity: suggestion
48	```
49	
50	**What happened.** A prior audit suggested a service-layer WS-message spec should parameterize over all 7 members of a discriminated-union code field, since it only tested 2 directly. A later fix exhaustively covered all 7 at the consumer layer (the component that maps each code to distinct UI text) instead. Re-examining the service's actual routing code showed it performs zero per-code branching -- it stores the whole message object regardless of which of the 7 values arrived. Parameterizing the service spec over all 7 values would have tested nothing the 2-value spec did not already prove; the router doesn't care which value it is.
51	
52	**Why it matters.** "Only N of M enum values are tested at this layer" is not automatically a gap. Whether it is a gap depends on whether that layer's code varies its behavior by value. Flagging it reflexively, without checking for branching, sends fix effort to the wrong file and can produce redundant tests that inflate a suite without adding assurance.
53	
54	**Pattern to encode.** Before treating partial per-value coverage as a finding, check whether the flagged code path branches on the value at all. If it's a pure pass-through, the exhaustive check belongs at the nearest layer that actually discriminates.
55

7	---
8

60	
61	## Architecture Patterns
62	
63	### Standalone components only
64	No `NgModule`. New code uses `standalone: true` (the default in Angular 21+). Components, directives, and pipes import their own dependencies via the `imports` array.
65	
66	### Signals for reactive state
67	- Component state: `signal()`, `computed()`, `linkedSignal()`.
68	- Async: `resource()` / `httpResource()` (Angular 20+). Falls back to `toSignal(observable$)` when interop with RxJS is required.
69	- Forms: signal-based forms (`Control` from `@angular/forms/signals`) for new code; existing reactive forms (`FormGroup`) are tolerated but new feature work uses signals.
70	- Do NOT use `BehaviorSubject` for component-local state. Use `signal()`.
71	
72	### OnPush change detection
73	Every new component declares `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`. The default `Default` strategy is forbidden in new code; it costs performance and hides re-render bugs.
74	
75	### Dependency injection
76	- `inject()` function inside the constructor body or as a class field. Constructor parameter injection is the older style; new code uses `inject()`.
77	- `providedIn: 'root'` for app-wide services. Feature-scoped services use a feature-local provider.
78	
79	### Routing
80	Lazy-load every feature route via `loadComponent` / `loadChildren`. Eager imports are reserved for the shell.

93	The pinned client version lives in `wopr.yml` (`api_contract.pinned_generator_version`) and must match `package.json`. If a needed operation is missing from the schema, the coder adds it in the same REQ.

100	- Theme tokens are CSS custom properties in `src/styles.scss`; components reference tokens, never raw color values.
101	- Global CSS is forbidden except for resets in the shell.

105	## Anti-Patterns (auditor surfaces these as BLOCKERs)
106	
107	- `@Component` without `changeDetection: OnPush` in new code.
108	- `NgModule` usage in new code.
109	- Hand-written GraphQL operation strings, HTTP calls, or schema type copies instead of `generateClient<Schema>()`.
110	- Hand-edits to `amplify_outputs.json`.
111	- Client code that writes game state the server must decide.
112	- Process or history comments in product source: REQ numbers, audit findings, rulings, learning IDs, dates, or narratives of how the code came to be. Comments explain only non-obvious code.

## Audit Report - REQ-ARC-3 Game rules and server authority
### Date / Auditor: 2026-10-28 / crew-auditor / Build: `tsc -p amplify/tsconfig.json` clean; `ng build` FAILS (environmental, see W1) / Test Results: 86 passed, 0 failed (2 files; 84 in game-rules.spec.ts)

## PR Readiness Verdict: UNBLOCKED
Zero BLOCKERs. Warnings below should be routed before or with the commit.

### BLOCKERS
None.

### WARNINGS
- **W1. `ng build` fails; recorded `gate: PASS` waives coder-spec gate condition 1 without saying so.** `src/main.ts:3` imports `../amplify_outputs.json` (TS2307). Independently verified: `src/main.ts` is unmodified vs HEAD, `amplify_outputs.json` is not tracked, and coder-spec "Source Layout" says it is generated and not committed. The failure is therefore pre-existing, environmental and not attributable to REQ-ARC-3. The operator forbids `ampx`, so it cannot be cleared here. Classification: WARNING (not BLOCKER). The log discloses the failure honestly, but `coverage_status ... gate: PASS` (implementation-tracking.md:84) should read "PASS, condition 1 (ng build) waived: missing generated amplify_outputs.json". Re-run `ng build` once the outputs file exists.
- **W2. `WINNING_LINES` is not frozen and `applyMove` aliases its entries into the returned state** (`amplify/shared/game-rules.ts:41`, `:119`). `result.line` in an accepted-move state is the module's own array element. A caller who mutates it at runtime (the `readonly` is type-level only) corrupts win detection for every later game in that process. This undercuts the "server is sole authority" intent and is inconsistent with `readAuthoritativeState`, which deep-copies and freezes. No test catches it, since `line` is only compared with `toEqual`. Fix: freeze the table and its rows, or copy the line in `applyMove`.
- **W3. AC5 is only partly delivered, but REQ-ARC-3 is marked whole `Implemented`.** The "source of truth over any live notification" clause has no code or test here. The scoping is honest and consistent: the scout contract and the log both call it a server-layer concern. But the status cell (implementation-tracking.md:58) carries no deferral note. Record explicitly that this clause (and the persisted "read at any time" surface) is deferred to the REQ that adds the read/subscription operations (REQ-ARC-4 per coder-spec API rule 3). Ready to merge as a pure-module REQ only on that understanding.
- **W4. Stale/contradictory tracking text.**
  - Header `Last updated: 2026-09-26 (fresh rebuild; baseline set, nothing built)` (line 3) contradicts the implemented REQ.
  - Gap Analysis row (line 73) has Baseline cell `✅ Implemented`, while its own narrative says the scout found it ALIGNED with `⏳ Pending`. The cell and narrative disagree (checklist item 1).
  - Line 75 says `Run mode: gap_analysis` for a crew run.

### SUGGESTIONS
- S1. `tsconfig.spec.json` is outside the scout's `files_touched` (the scout only anticipated `angular.json`). The change is minimal and justified (type-checks the amplify specs under the spec tsconfig), but record it as accepted drift.
- S2. Propose spec amendments (spec_writes OFF): tester spec should name the `angular.json` test `include` (`"../amplify/**/*.spec.ts"`, globs resolve relative to `sourceRoot`) and a Test File Layout row for `amplify/shared/*.spec.ts`; coder-spec Source Layout needs an `amplify/shared/` row; both specs say `wopr.yml` where the repo uses `kitt.yml`; coder-spec build gate should say what to do when `amplify_outputs.json` is absent.
- S3. `applyMove` trusts runtime shape (`playerId` non-string, `cell` undefined). The cell check covers `undefined` via `Number.isInteger`, and the participant check covers other types. Behavior is safe as is; no action.

### PASSED
- Item 1 (traceability, status vs reality): module and spec exist and match the Implemented claim, except the W3/W4 notes.
- Item 2 (pattern compliance): no Angular/GraphQL anti-patterns apply; no generated files touched; `amplify/data/resource.ts` unchanged. `.spec.ts` naming, Vitest imports, no network, no snapshots, no `it.skip`.

## LRN-2026-10-28-a: A "pure" rules function that returns a module-level constant by reference lets callers corrupt the rules

```meta
date: 2026-10-28
project: arcade
stack: [typescript, vitest, amplify-gen2]
req: [REQ-ARC-3]
auditor_run: AUDIT_REPORT.md@2026-10-28
severity: warning
```

**What happened.** A pure game-rules module returned the winning line inside each new state by reference to its own `WINNING_LINES` table. The table was only `readonly` at the type level. The separate read function deep-copied and froze, but the move function did not. 100% coverage and 16 per-line tests passed, since every test compared the line with `toEqual` and none mutated it.

**Why it matters.** Types do not stop runtime writes. One caller mutating a returned `result.line` changes win detection for every later game in the process. Tests that only assert equality cannot see aliasing.

**Pattern to encode.** When an authority module returns data derived from a module-level constant table, either freeze the table (and its rows) at definition or copy on return. Add one test that mutates a returned value and then re-runs the rule. Review every return path of a "pure" function for shared references, not only the read API.

REQ-ARC-3 is done. The audit came back **UNBLOCKED** with no blockers and four warnings. Nothing is committed: this session's instructions didn't ask for a commit, and the old "commit after each UNBLOCKED REQ" rule came from the September session.

**What was built**
- `amplify/shared/game-rules.ts` is the rules module. It has five ordered rejection reasons: `not_a_participant`, `game_finished`, `not_your_turn`, `invalid_cell`, `cell_occupied`. Win detection covers all 8 lines and reports the winner and the line; a full board with no line is a draw. `readAuthoritativeState` returns a read-only copy of the state.
- `amplify/shared/game-rules.spec.ts` has 84 tests, and each of the 5 acceptance criteria maps to named tests.
- `angular.json` and `tsconfig.spec.json` now include `amplify/**` specs. Without that change, `ng test` never ran the new tests.

**Checks I ran myself**
- `ng test --coverage` passes 86 of 86 tests, with 100% line and branch coverage.
- `tsc` on the amplify project and `eslint` are both clean.
- The auditor broke the code on purpose five ways in a throwaway copy, and the tests caught every one.

**Decisions you should know about**

**Pattern to encode:** before trusting any client-asserted identity field (a body `sub`, a JWT claim read without signature verification, a session id used as if it were proof), ask: does this action's correctness depend on WHICH identity is calling (not just "some" valid one), and is the effect account-scoped and durable/irreversible?
